text: Track 8.1 Thank you for coming tonight. Let's start with some quick questions for everyone. When was the last time you took out money from a cash machine? When was the last time you made a payment with cash? In other words, when did you last use coins and notes to buy something? Probably not for some time. It seems that every day more and more shops are making the decision to have customers use cards or mobile payment. Some people think this means that we won't use cash anymore. The end of cash they call it. Personally, I'm not convinced for a couple of reasons. First of all, we've used physical money like coins and notes for a very, very long time. Some coins are thousands of years old. It is easy to carry and it's very reliable. You can use it anywhere, whether you want to buy a bar of chocolates at the corner shop or do your weekly shopping in a big supermarket chain. Using cash is also a way of keeping your money private. That is, you can use it without anyone checking on you. Bitcoin, a digital kind of money, which is managed by people and not the government, is similar to cash in this way. But it isn't safe and it's difficult to use. People use credit and debit cards all the time, but they immediately connect what you buy to who you are. To use online payments, you have to have an app and an account. To put it another way, technology doesn't have the secret thing that cash has. Cash is private and I like that. However, the main reason I don't agree that this is the end of cash is our relationship with it. People look at coins and notes in a different way from electronic money. They both have the same value, but because you can see cash and hold it, it makes it feel like you own it more. In fact, when I have cash, I spend it in a more responsible way. When I buy things with my card, I use it without thinking. Humans have a strong relationship with coins and notes, so I don't think we'd be able to give up cash easily anyway. Cash just feels safer and this is something that digital money can't offer at the moment. If there's some kind of financial crisis or a natural disaster when there's no power, I'm sure most of you would rather have the money in your hand, right? I know I would. To sum up, I don't think that the end of cash is happening soon. I just don't see the other options as better. For now anyway. And our relationship with cash means it will be in our pockets for some time to come.
